title: Conformal Prediction with Paraphrase-Aware Scoring for LLM Uncertainty Quantification
claim: Standard conformal scores flip prediction sets under meaning-preserving rewording; aggregating paraphrases through a proxy model keeps sets stable.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; problem top, our method bottom; matching worked example
description: A 2x2 grid of colored, bordered panels built on one running example, "What is the capital of France?". Panel A (blue, top left) explains conformal prediction basics in three steps: multiple-choice options, nonconformity scores shown as bars, then a calibrated threshold q-hat that gives the prediction set {Paris}. Panel B (red, top right) shows the problem: the original question and a reworded one give different bar scores and thresholds, so the prediction set changes from {Paris} to {Paris, Lyon}. A red banner reads "Same meaning, different prediction set". Panel C (purple, bottom left) is the method pipeline. A user question is paraphrased internally, each paraphrase goes through LLM embedding, and a proxy model outputs distributions that are aggregated. Panel D (green, bottom right) shows the paraphrase-aware scores giving {Paris} for both inputs. A green banner reads "Semantic invariance → more stable prediction sets". Color coding (red for the problem, green for the benefit) guides the eye.
caption: Prior scores are sensitive to rewording or paraphrasing of input question (denoted as $\mathcal{T}$), producing larger prediction sets (Panel A and B). {Our PA framework aggregates multiple paraphrases with a proxy model to reduce score and prediction-set sensitivity to rewording (Panel C and D).}
abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) for large language models (LLMs) aims to provide reliable measures of predictive confidence, yet current methods are often unstable under meaning-preserving perturbations. Semantically equivalent paraphrases can induce substantial variability in predictive confidence, even for methods with formal guarantees, such as conformal prediction. To address this issue, we propose a paraphrase-aware UQ framework robust to semantic rewordings. Our approach trains a lightweight proxy model on LLM hidden states and aggregates its predictions across paraphrases to construct label-wise nonconformity scores. Under score exchangeability, conformal calibration retains marginal coverage. This guarantee can also hold under test-only rewording, provided that the paraphrase pipeline satisfies an additional distributional alignment condition. We evaluate three settings (normal, fully reworded, and semi-reworded) which apply rewording to neither dataset, both calibration and test datasets, or only the test dataset, respectively. Across seven multiple-choice QA benchmarks and multiple model families, our method produces compact prediction sets with empirical coverage generally near the nominal target, even in the semi-reworded setting. Ablation studies show that the learned proxy accounts for most of the reduction in set size, while paraphrase-augmented training and inference-time aggregation improve stability under rewording. Code is available at https://github.com/Raina-Xin/PA_Score.
